=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:lines 78, 237-242 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Verdict matching is round-agnostic, so a verdict for an earlier round on the same head SHA can cause a newer findings handoff to be treated as answered.
  WHY: The checker can fall through to normal PR logic instead of reporting `state: review-round`, leaving new findings without a stage session; severity was MAJOR across these reports, and deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro disputes the separate empty-head-SHA finding by noting that `main()` catches `ValueError`.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:line 123 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The findings handoff comment includes the verdict marker format with the real head SHA as instruction text, so the checker can treat the handoff itself as an answering verdict.
  WHY: The checker scans both marker formats in the same comment, setting `latest_handoff` and `answered=True` together, so it never reports `state: review-round`.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:lines 210-212, 226-228, 297 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: An empty head SHA on a Claude-fixer PR raises an uncaught `ValueError` instead of returning the structured exit-2 error.
  WHY: The reports say the exception bypasses the structured error path; severity ranged from MAJOR to NIT, and deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro disputes the finding, noting that `main()` catches `ValueError`.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:lines 108-133, 228 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `gh_api_list` raises `ReadError` after 10 pages, preventing the fixer checker from reading comments once a PR exceeds 1000 comments.
  WHY: The checker retries without seeing earlier handoff markers, which can cause repeated failures or route the PR to a block stage after consecutive errors.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:lines 133-135 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The call site for `_check_claude_fixer_pr` does not handle `ReadError`.
  WHY: A `ReadError` from `gh_api_list` can crash the checker instead of producing the expected structured exit-2 error response.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:lines 718-720, 741-745, around line 763 in the post-PR-diff line numbers | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Claude-fixer mode is selected solely by the `claude/implement-plan-` head-ref prefix, so an unrelated PR with a colliding branch name enters that mode.
  WHY: Such a PR skips the GPT editor and related workflow steps and may wait for a Claude session that will not arrive.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:line 50; `CLAUDE_FIXER_ROUND_INDEX` arithmetic
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: An invalid `CLAUDE_FIXER_ROUND_INDEX` can produce a handoff with `round=0`.
  WHY: The round index is not validated as an integer before arithmetic and interpolation.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:gate block "claude_fixer_awaiting_session" branch (around line 763 in the post-PR-diff line numbers)
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `claude_fixer_awaiting_session` skip has no age limit for a handoff.
  WHY: If the stage session crashes after posting a handoff, subsequent dispatches can be skipped indefinitely until the 24-hour safety-net reminder.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:`SECURITY_AUDIT_SKIP_IF_UNCHANGED` block
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Branch audits have no branch-audit-specific skip check, so a future change that records a branch tip as the last-audited SHA could silently make an unchanged branch audit skip.
  WHY: The report says the documented behavior holds today only because the current comparison uses the default-branch marker.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:FIXER_HANDOFF_RE (line 76); FIXER_VERDICT_RE (line 78); `.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` step 7a
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Adding round tracking to verdict markers would change the marker format and must be paired with the command-side verdict emission update.
  WHY: Existing tests and session output assume the no-round format, so changing only the checker could leave it unable to recognize verdicts emitted by existing sessions.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:line 124; `review_autofix.yml` line ~3713
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A session that uses `[claude-autofix]` for a conflict-resolution commit can have that commit counted as an autofix iteration.
  WHY: The iteration counter counts `[claude-autofix]` commits, potentially spending a round on a conflict resolve and causing premature `ai:review-blocked`.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:lines 78 (FIXER_VERDICT_RE) and 237-242 (loop body in _check_claude_fixer_pr) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: FIXER_VERDICT_RE captures only the head SHA, not the review round number, so a verdict for an earlier round on the same head can cause a newer findings handoff to be treated as answered.
  WHY: The checker returns None instead of reporting `state: review-round`, so the review-round stage session is never started and new findings go unaddressed.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:lines 108-123 (gh_api_list) and 228 (call site in _check_claude_fixer_pr) | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: gh_api_list raises ReadError with "pagination exceeded 10 pages" after 1000 comments.
  WHY: The checker repeats the failure on every cycle instead of recognizing a handoff marker on an earlier page or falling through.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:lines 741-745 (CLAUDE_FIXER mode activation based on head ref prefix) | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: Any PR with a head ref starting with claude/implement-plan- is placed in Claude-fixer mode.
  WHY: A branch-name collision can cause a PR to wait for a session that will never arrive.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:211-212 (inside _check_claude_fixer_pr) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Unhandled ValueError when head_sha is empty.
  WHY: `_check_claude_fixer_pr` raises a ValueError if head_sha is empty, but the caller `check_pr` does not catch it. This crashes the checker script with an unhandled exception instead of exiting with the structured JSON error response expected by the orchestrator.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:240-242 (_check_claude_fixer_pr) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Verdict marker checking is round-agnostic for a given head SHA.
  WHY: The verdict marker from an earlier round is still detected as answering a new hand-off, causing the checker to miss the `review-round` state and fall back to normal PR logic.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:133-135 (called from check_pr) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Call site for _check_claude_fixer_pr lacks ReadError handling.
  WHY: If `gh_api_list` raises a ReadError, the checker script crashes instead of producing the expected structured exit-2 error response.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:718-720 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: Claude-fixer mode uses a branch name prefix collision risk as its identifier.
  WHY: An unrelated PR using a colliding branch name would have its GPT editor and resolver skipped, potentially stalling its review.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:line 76 (FIXER_VERDICT_RE) and lines237-242 (verdict matching loop in _check_claude_fixer_pr) | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The verdict regex captures only the head SHA, and the matching loop sets `answered = True` for any verdict comment containing the marker for the current head SHA.
  WHY: A verdict for round 1 followed by a round 2 hand-off for the same head causes the checker to fall through instead of reporting `state: review-round`.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:line228 (`if not head_sha: raise ValueError("PR head sha is empty")`) and the main() exception handler at line 297 | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: `_check_claude_fixer_pr` raises a bare `ValueError` for an empty head SHA.
  WHY: `ValueError` propagates as an unhandled traceback instead of the structured `{"done": false, "error": ...}` JSON with exit code 2.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:`gh_api_list` at lines 119-133, MAX_PAGINATED_API_PAGES = 10 | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: `gh_api_list` paginates in 100-item pages and raises `ReadError("pagination exceeded 10 pages")` after 1000 items.
  WHY: The checker cannot see an early hand-off comment after the pagination cap and repeated failures can route the PR to a block stage.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh:line 50 (`head_sha="${HEAD_SHA:-}"` declared at line 41 is used unquoted in the `[[ "${HEAD_SHA:-}" =~ ... ]]` check at line 50, then `${claude_fixer_run_url}` interpolates `${HEAD_SHA}` into the comment body without further validation between line 50 and the marker-echoing `echo`s) | confidence=[1]
  PROBLEM: If a future caller sets `CLAUDE_FIXER_ROUND_INDEX` to a non-integer or whitespace value, the arithmetic can fall back to `0` and post a hand-off with `round=0`.
  WHY: The round index path is not guarded, although the reported `round=0` hand-off is correctly parsed by the checker.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:gate block "claude_fixer_awaiting_session" branch (around line 763 in the post-PR-diff line numbers) | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The `claude_fixer_awaiting_session` skip fires for any hand-off for the current head, regardless of age.
  WHY: A crashed stage session can leave subsequent workflow dispatches skipped until the 24-hour safety-net reminder.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:`SECURITY_AUDIT_SKIP_IF_UNCHANGED` block | confidence=[1]
  PROBLEM: Branch audits have no branch-audit-specific skip check.
  WHY: The report says behavior holds today, but a future change that records the branch tip as the last-audited SHA could silently break the "branch audit never skips" promise.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:FIXER_HANDOFF_RE (line 76) captures `(kind, head, round)`; FIXER_VERDICT_RE (line 78) captures only `(head)`.
  PROBLEM: Adding round tracking to verdicts would be a backward-incompatible wire-format change unless the command-side verdict emission is updated too.
  WHY: Existing
